problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+3y=2{e}^{2x}+{e}^{5x}
$$

has the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{-3x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.

${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

We see that the right-hand side is $2{e}^{2x}+{e}^{5x},$ and neither ${e}^{2x}$ nor ${e}^{5x}$ is a term in the complementary solution, so we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha {e}^{2x}+\beta {e}^{5x},
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined.

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=2\alpha {e}^{2x}+5\beta {e}^{5x}.
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(2\alpha {e}^{2x}+5\beta {e}^{5x})+3(\alpha {e}^{2x}+\beta {e}^{5x}) & =2{e}^{2x}+{e}^{5x} \\ (2\alpha +3\alpha ){e}^{2x}+(5\beta +3\beta ){e}^{5x} & =2{e}^{2x}+{e}^{5x} \\ 5\alpha {e}^{2x}+8\beta {e}^{5x} & =2{e}^{2x}+{e}^{5x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients of ${e}^{2x}$ and ${e}^{5x},$ respectively, gives

$$
5\alpha =2,\,8\beta =1.
$$

So, we have

$$
\alpha =\frac{2}{5},\,\beta =\frac{1}{8}.
$$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\frac{2}{5}{e}^{2x}+\frac{1}{8}{e}^{5x}.
$$
